text: And if the ear shall say, Because I am not the eye, I am not of the body; is it therefore not of the body?

title: I Corinthians 12:17
text: If the whole body [were] an eye, where [were] the hearing? If the whole [were] hearing, where [were] the smelling?

title: I Corinthians 12:18
text: But now hath God set the members every one of them in the body, as it hath pleased him.

title: I Corinthians 12:19
text: And if they were all one member, where [were] the body?

title: I Corinthians 12:20
text: But now [are they] many members, yet but one body.

title: I Corinthians 12:21
text: And the eye cannot say unto the hand, I have no need of thee: nor again the head to the feet, I have no need of you.

title: I Corinthians 12:22
text: Nay, much more those members of the body, which seem to be more feeble, are necessary:

title: I Corinthians 12:23
text: And those [members] of the body, which we think to be less honourable, upon these we bestow more abundant honour; and our uncomely [parts] have more abundant comeliness. {bestow: or, put on}

title: I Corinthians 12:24
text: For our comely [parts] have no need: but God hath tempered the body together, having given more abundant honour to that [part] which lacked:

title: I Corinthians 12:25
text: That there should be no schism in the body; but [that] the members should have the same care one for another. {schism: or, division}

title: I Corinthians 12:26
text: And whether one member suffer, all the members suffer with it; or one member be honoured, all the members rejoice with it.

title: I Corinthians 12:27
text: ¶Now ye are the body of Christ, and members in particular.

title: I Corinthians 12:28
text: And God hath set some in the church, first apostles, secondarily prophets, thirdly teachers, after that miracles, then gifts of healings, helps, governments, diversities of tongues. {diversities: or, kinds}

title: I Corinthians 12:29
text: [Are] all apostles? [are] all prophets? [are] all teachers? [are] all workers of miracles? {workers...: or, powers?}

title: I Corinthians 12:30
text: Have all the gifts of healing? do all speak with tongues? do all interpret?

title: I Corinthians 12:31
text: But covet earnestly the best gifts: and yet shew I unto you a more excellent way.

title: I Corinthians 13:1
text: ¶Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, and have not charity, I am become [as] sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal.

title: I Corinthians 13:2
text: And though I have [the gift of] prophecy, and understand all mysteries, and all knowledge; and though I have all faith, so that I could remove mountains, and have not charity, I am nothing.

title: I Corinthians 13:3
text: And though I bestow all my goods to feed [the poor], and though I give my body to be burned, and have not charity, it profiteth me nothing.

title: I Corinthians 13:4
text: ¶Charity suffereth long, [and] is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up, {vaunteth...: or, is not rash}

title: I Corinthians 13:5
text: Doth not behave itself unseemly, seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil;

title: I Corinthians 13:6
text: Rejoiceth not in iniquity, but rejoiceth in the truth; {in the truth: or, with the truth}

title: I Corinthians 13:7
text: Beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things.

title: I Corinthians 13:8
text: ¶Charity never faileth: but whether [there be] prophecies, they shall fail; whether [there be] tongues, they shall cease; whether [there be] knowledge, it shall vanish away. {fail: Gr. vanish away}

title: I Corinthians 13:9
text: For we know in part, and we prophesy in part.

title: I Corinthians 13:10
text: But when that which is perfect is come, then that which is in part shall be done away. {done away: Gr. vanish away}

title: I Corinthians 13:11
text: When I was a child, I spake as a child, I understood as a child, I thought as a child: but when I became a man, I put away childish things. {thought: or, reasoned} {put away: Gr. vanish away}

title: I Corinthians 13:12
text: For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known. {darkly: Gr. in a riddle}

title: I Corinthians 13:13
text: And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these [is] charity.

title: I Corinthians 14:1
text: ¶Follow after charity, and desire spiritual [gifts], but rather that ye may prophesy.

title: I Corinthians 14:2
text: For he that speaketh in an [unknown] tongue speaketh not unto men, but unto God: for no man understandeth [him]; howbeit in the spirit he speaketh mysteries. {understandeth: Gr. heareth}

title: I Corinthians 14:3
text: But he that prophesieth speaketh unto men [to] edification, and exhortation, and comfort.

title: I Corinthians 14:4
text: He that speaketh in an [unknown] tongue edifieth himself; but he that prophesieth edifieth the church.

title: I Corinthians 14:5
text: I would that ye all spake with tongues, but rather that ye prophesied: for greater [is] he that prophesieth than he that speaketh with tongues, except he interpret, that the church may receive edifying.

title: I Corinthians 14:6
text: ¶ Now, brethren, if I come unto you speaking with tongues, what shall I profit you, except I shall speak to you either by revelation, or by knowledge, or by prophesying, or by doctrine?

title: I Corinthians 14:7
text: And even things without life giving sound, whether pipe or harp, except they give a distinction in the sounds, how shall it be known what is piped or harped? {sounds: or, tunes}

title: I Corinthians 14:8
text: For if the trumpet give an uncertain sound, who shall prepare himself to the battle?

title: I Corinthians 14:9
text: So likewise ye, except ye utter by the tongue words easy to be understood, how shall it be known what is spoken? for ye shall speak into the air. {easy...: Gr. significant}

title: I Corinthians 14:10
text: There are, it may be, so many kinds of voices in the world, and none of them [is] without signification.

title: I Corinthians 14:11
text: Therefore if I know not the meaning of the voice, I shall be unto him that speaketh a barbarian, and he that speaketh [shall be] a barbarian unto me.

title: I Corinthians 14:12
text: Even so ye, forasmuch as ye are zealous of spiritual [gifts], seek that ye may excel to the edifying of the church. {of spiritual gifts: Gr. of spirits}

title: I Corinthians 14:13
text: Wherefore let him that speaketh in an [unknown] tongue pray that he may interpret.

title: I Corinthians 14:14
text: For if I pray in an [unknown] tongue, my spirit prayeth, but my understanding is unfruitful.

title: I Corinthians 14:15
text: ¶What is it then? I will pray with the spirit, and I will pray with the understanding also: I will sing with the spirit, and I will sing with the understanding also.

title: I Corinthians 14:16
text: Else when thou shalt bless with the spirit, how shall he that occupieth the room of the unlearned say Amen at thy giving of thanks, seeing he understandeth not what thou sayest?

title: I Corinthians 14:17
text: For thou verily givest thanks well, but the other is not edified.

title: I Corinthians 14:18
text: I thank my God, I speak with tongues more than ye all:

title: I Corinthians 14:19
text: Yet in the church I had rather speak five words with my understanding, that [by my voice] I might teach others also, than ten thousand words in an [unknown] tongue.

title: I Corinthians 14:20
text: Brethren, be not children in understanding: howbeit in malice be ye children, but in understanding be men. {men: Gr. perfect, or, of a ripe age}

title: I Corinthians 14:21
text: ¶In the law it is written, With [men of] other tongues and other lips will I speak unto this people; and yet for all that will they not hear me, saith the Lord.

title: I Corinthians 14:22
text: Wherefore tongues are for a sign, not to them that believe, but to them that believe not: but prophesying [serveth] not for them that believe not, but for them which believe.

title: I Corinthians 14:23
text: If therefore the whole church be come together into one place, and all speak with tongues, and there come in [those that are] unlearned, or unbelievers, will they not say that ye are mad?

title: I Corinthians 14:24
text: But if all prophesy, and there come in one that believeth not, or [one] unlearned, he is convinced of all, he is judged of all:

title: I Corinthians 14:25
text: And thus are the secrets of his heart made manifest; and so falling down on [his] face he will worship God, and report that God is in you of a truth.

title: I Corinthians 14:26
text: ¶How is it then, brethren? when ye come together, every one of you hath a psalm, hath a doctrine, hath a tongue, hath a revelation, hath an interpretation. Let all things be done unto edifying.

title: I Corinthians 14:27
text: If any man speak in an [unknown] tongue, [let it be] by two, or at the most [by] three, and [that] by course; and let one interpret. {two...: by two or three sentences separately}

title: I Corinthians 14:28
text: But if there be no interpreter, let him keep silence in the church; and let him speak to himself, and to God.

title: I Corinthians 14:29
text: Let the prophets speak two or three, and let the other judge.

title: I Corinthians 14:30
text: If [any thing] be revealed to another that sitteth by, let the first hold his peace.

title: I Corinthians 14:31
text: For ye may all prophesy one by one, that all may learn, and all may be comforted.

title: I Corinthians 14:32
text: And the spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets.

title: I Corinthians 14:33
text: For God is not [the author] of confusion, but of peace, as in all churches of the saints. {confusion: Gr. tumult, or, unquietness}

title: I Corinthians 14:34
text: ¶Let your women keep silence in the churches: for it is not permitted unto them to speak; but [they are commanded] to be under obedience, as also saith the law.

title: I Corinthians 14:35
text: And if they will learn any thing, let them ask their husbands at home: for it is a shame for women to speak in the church.

title: I Corinthians 14:36
text: ¶What? came the word of God out from you? or came it unto you only?

title: I Corinthians 14:37
text: If any man think himself to be a prophet, or spiritual, let him acknowledge that the things that I write unto you are the commandments of the Lord.

title: I Corinthians 14:38
text: But if any man be ignorant, let him be ignorant.

title: I Corinthians 14:39
text: Wherefore, brethren, covet to prophesy, and forbid not to speak with tongues.

title: I Corinthians 14:40
text: Let all things be done decently and in order.

title: I Corinthians 15:1
text: ¶Moreover, brethren, I declare unto you the gospel which I preached unto you, which also ye have received, and wherein ye stand;

title: I Corinthians 15:2
text: By which also ye are saved, if ye keep in memory what I preached unto you, unless ye have believed in vain. {keep...: or, hold fast} {what: Gr. by what speech}

title: I Corinthians 15:3
text: For I delivered unto you first of all that which I also received, how that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures;

title: I Corinthians 15:4
text: And that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures:

title: I Corinthians 15:5
text: And that he was seen of Cephas, then of the twelve:

title: I Corinthians 15:6
text: After that, he was seen of above five hundred brethren at once; of whom the greater part remain unto this present, but some are fallen asleep.

title: I Corinthians 15:7
text: After that, he was seen of James; then of all the apostles.

title: I Corinthians 15:8
text: And last of all he was seen of me also, as of one born out of due time. {one...: or, an abortive}

title: I Corinthians 15:9
text: For I am the least of the apostles, that am not meet to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.

title: I Corinthians 15:10
text: But by the grace of God I am what I am: and his grace which [was bestowed] upon me was not in vain; but I laboured more abundantly than they all: yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me.

title: I Corinthians 15:11
text: Therefore whether [it were] I or they, so we preach, and so ye believed.

title: I Corinthians 15:12
text: ¶Now if Christ be preached that he rose from the dead, how say some among you that there is no resurrection of the dead?

title: I Corinthians 15:13
text: But if there be no resurrection of the dead, then is Christ not risen:

title: I Corinthians 15:14
text: And if Christ be not risen, then [is] our preaching vain, and your faith [is] also vain.

title: I Corinthians 15:15
text: Yea, and we are found false witnesses of God; because we have testified of God that he raised up Christ: whom he raised not up, if so be that the dead rise not.

title: I Corinthians 15:16
text: For if the dead rise not, then is not Christ raised:

title: I Corinthians 15:17
text: And if Christ be not raised, your faith [is] vain; ye are yet in your sins.

title: I Corinthians 15:18
text: Then they also which are fallen asleep in Christ are perished.

title: I Corinthians 15:19
text: If in this life only we have hope in Christ, we are of all men most miserable.

title: I Corinthians 15:20
text: ¶But now is Christ risen from the dead, [and] become the firstfruits of them that slept.

title: I Corinthians 15:21
text: For since by man [came] death, by man [came] also the resurrection of the dead.

title: I Corinthians 15:22
text: For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive.

title: I Corinthians 15:23
text: But every man in his own order: Christ the firstfruits; afterward they that are Christ's at his coming.

title: I Corinthians 15:24
text: Then [cometh] the end, when he shall have delivered up the kingdom to God, even the Father; when he shall have put down all rule and all authority and power.

title: I Corinthians 15:25
text: For he must reign, till he hath put all enemies under his feet.

title: I Corinthians 15:26
text: The last enemy [that] shall be destroyed [is] death.

title: I Corinthians 15:27
text: For he hath put all things under his feet. But when he saith all things are put under [him, it is] manifest that he is excepted, which did put all things under him.

title: I Corinthians 15:28
text: And when all things shall be subdued unto him, then shall the Son also himself be subject unto him that put all things under him, that God may be all in all.

title: I Corinthians 15:29
text: Else what shall they do which are baptized for the dead, if the dead rise not at all? why are they then baptized for the dead?

title: I Corinthians 15:30
text: And why stand we in jeopardy every hour?

title: I Corinthians 15:31
text: I protest by your rejoicing which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord, I die daily. {your: some read, our}

title: I Corinthians 15:32
text: If after the manner of men I have fought with beasts at Ephesus, what advantageth it me, if the dead rise not? let us eat and drink; for to morrow we die. {after...: or, to speak after the manner of men}

title: I Corinthians 15:33
text: Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners.

title: I Corinthians 15:34
text: Awake to righteousness, and sin not; for some have not the knowledge of God: I speak [this] to your shame.

title: I Corinthians 15:35
text: ¶But some [man] will say, How are the dead raised up? and with what body do they come?

title: I Corinthians 15:36
text: [Thou] fool, that which thou sowest is not quickened, except it die:

title: I Corinthians 15:37
text: And that which thou sowest, thou sowest not that body that shall be, but bare grain, it may chance of wheat, or of some other [grain]:

title: I Corinthians 15:38
text: But God giveth it a body as it hath pleased him, and to every seed his own body.

title: I Corinthians 15:39
text: All flesh [is] not the same flesh: but [there is] one [kind of] flesh of men, another flesh of beasts, another of fishes, [and] another of birds.

title: I Corinthians 15:40
text: [There are] also celestial bodies, and bodies terrestrial: but the glory of the celestial [is] one, and the [glory] of the terrestrial [is] another.

title: I Corinthians 15:41
text: [There is] one glory of the sun, and another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars: for [one] star differeth from [another] star in glory.

title: I Corinthians 15:42
text: So also [is] the resurrection of the dead. It is sown in corruption; it is raised in incorruption:

title: I Corinthians 15:43
text: It is sown in dishonour; it is raised in glory: it is sown in weakness; it is raised in power:

title: I Corinthians 15:44
text: It is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body. There is a natural body, and there is a spiritual body.

title: I Corinthians 15:45
text: And so it is written, The first man Adam was made a living soul; the last Adam [was made] a quickening spirit.

title: I Corinthians 15:46
text: Howbeit that [was] not first which is spiritual, but that which is natural; and afterward that which is spiritual.

title: I Corinthians 15:47
text: The first man [is] of the earth, earthy: the second man [is] the Lord from heaven.

title: I Corinthians 15:48
text: As [is] the earthy, such [are] they also that are earthy: and as [is] the heavenly, such [are] they also that are heavenly.

title: I Corinthians 15:49
text: And as we have borne the image of the earthy, we shall also bear the image of the heavenly.

title: I Corinthians 15:50
text: Now this I say, brethren, that flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God; neither doth corruption inherit incorruption.

title: I Corinthians 15:51
text: ¶Behold, I shew you a mystery; We shall not all sleep, but we shall all be changed,

title: I Corinthians 15:52
text: In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump: for the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed.

title: I Corinthians 15:53
text: For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal [must] put on immortality.

title: I Corinthians 15:54
text: So when this corruptible shall have put on incorruption, and this mortal shall have put on immortality, then shall be brought to pass the saying that is written, Death is swallowed up in victory.

title: I Corinthians 15:55
text: O death, where [is] thy sting? O grave, where [is] thy victory? {grave: or, hell}

title: I Corinthians 15:56
text: The sting of death [is] sin; and the strength of sin [is] the law.

title: I Corinthians 15:57
text: But thanks [be] to God, which giveth us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.

title: I Corinthians 15:58
text: ¶Therefore, my beloved brethren, be ye stedfast, unmoveable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, forasmuch as ye know that your labour is not in vain in the Lord.

title: I Corinthians 16:1
text: ¶Now concerning the collection for the saints, as I have given order to the churches of Galatia, even so do ye.

title: I Corinthians 16:2
text: Upon the first [day] of the week let every one of you lay by him in store, as [God] hath prospered him, that there be no gatherings when I come.

title: I Corinthians 16:3
text: And when I come, whomsoever ye shall approve by [your] letters, them will I send to bring your liberality unto Jerusalem. {liberality: Gr. gift}

title: I Corinthians 16:4
text: And if it be meet that I go also, they shall go with me.

title: I Corinthians 16:5
text: ¶Now I will come unto you, when I shall pass through Macedonia: for I do pass through Macedonia.

title: I Corinthians 16:6
text: And it may be that I will abide, yea, and winter with you, that ye may bring me on my journey whithersoever I go.

title: I Corinthians 16:7
text: For I will not see you now by the way; but I trust to tarry a while with you, if the Lord permit.

title: I Corinthians 16:8
text: But I will tarry at Ephesus until Pentecost.

title: I Corinthians 16:9
text: For a great door and effectual is opened unto me, and [there are] many adversaries.

title: I Corinthians 16:10
text: ¶Now if Timotheus come, see that he may be with you without fear: for he worketh the work of the Lord, as I also [do].

title: I Corinthians 16:11
text: Let no man therefore despise him: but conduct him forth in peace, that he may come unto me: for I look for him with the brethren.

title: I Corinthians 16:12
text: As touching [our] brother Apollos, I greatly desired him to come unto you with the brethren: but his will was not at all to come at this time; but he will come when he shall have convenient time.

title: I Corinthians 16:13
text: ¶Watch ye, stand fast in the faith, quit you like men, be strong.

title: I Corinthians 16:14
text: Let all your things be done with charity.

title: I Corinthians 16:15
text: I beseech you, brethren, (ye know the house of Stephanas, that it is the firstfruits of Achaia, and [that] they have addicted themselves to the ministry of the saints,)

title: I Corinthians 16:16
text: That ye submit yourselves unto such, and to every one that helpeth with [us], and laboureth.

title: I Corinthians 16:17
text: I am glad of the coming of Stephanas and Fortunatus and Achaicus: for that which was lacking on your part they have supplied.

title: I Corinthians 16:18
text: For they have refreshed my spirit and yours: therefore acknowledge ye them that are such.

title: I Corinthians 16:19
text: ¶The churches of Asia salute you. Aquila and Priscilla salute you much in the Lord, with the church that is in their house.

title: I Corinthians 16:20
text: All the brethren greet you. Greet ye one another with an holy kiss.

title: I Corinthians 16:21
text: The salutation of [me] Paul with mine own hand.

title: I Corinthians 16:22
text: If any man love not the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be Anathema Maranatha.

title: I Corinthians 16:23
text: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ [be] with you.

title: I Corinthians 16:24
text: My love [be] with you all in Christ Jesus. Amen. <<[The first [epistle] to the Corinthians was written from Philippi by Stephanas and Fortunatus and Achaicus and Timotheus.]>>

title: II Corinthians 1:1
text: ¶Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timothy [our] brother, unto the church of God which is at Corinth, with all the saints which are in all Achaia:

title: II Corinthians 1:2
text: Grace [be] to you and peace from God our Father, and [from] the Lord Jesus Christ.

title: II Corinthians 1:3
text: ¶Blessed [be] God, even the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies, and the God of all comfort;

title: II Corinthians 1:4
text: Who comforteth us in all our tribulation, that we may be able to comfort them which are in any trouble, by the comfort wherewith we ourselves are comforted of God.

title: II Corinthians 1:5
text: For as the sufferings of Christ abound in us, so our consolation also aboundeth by Christ.

title: II Corinthians 1:6
text: And whether we be afflicted, [it is] for your consolation and salvation, which is effectual in the enduring of the same sufferings which we also suffer: or whether we be comforted, [it is] for your consolation and salvation. {is effectual: or, is wrought}

title: II Corinthians 1:7
text: ¶And our hope of you [is] stedfast, knowing, that as ye are partakers of the sufferings, so [shall ye be] also of the consolation.

title: II Corinthians 1:8
text: For we would not, brethren, have you ignorant of our trouble which came to us in Asia, that we were pressed out of measure, above strength, insomuch that we despaired even of life:

title: II Corinthians 1:9
text: But we had the sentence of death in ourselves, that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God which raiseth the dead: {sentence: or, answer}

title: II Corinthians 1:10
text: Who delivered us from so great a death, and doth deliver: in whom we trust that he will yet deliver [us];

title: II Corinthians 1:11
text: Ye also helping together by prayer for us, that for the gift [bestowed] upon us by the means of many persons thanks may be given by many on our behalf.

title: II Corinthians 1:12
text: ¶For our rejoicing is this, the testimony of our conscience, that in simplicity and godly sincerity, not with fleshly wisdom, but by the grace of God, we have had our conversation in the world, and more abundantly to you-ward.

title: II Corinthians 1:13
text: For we write none other things unto you, than what ye read or acknowledge; and I trust ye shall acknowledge even to the end;

title: II Corinthians 1:14
text: As also ye have acknowledged us in part, that we are your rejoicing, even as ye also [are] ours in the day of the Lord Jesus.

title: II Corinthians 1:15
text: ¶And in this confidence I was minded to come unto you before, that ye might have a second benefit; {benefit: or, grace}

title: II Corinthians 1:16
text: And to pass by you into Macedonia, and to come again out of Macedonia unto you, and of you to be brought on my way toward Judaea.

title: II Corinthians 1:17
text: When I therefore was thus minded, did I use lightness? or the things that I purpose, do I purpose according to the flesh, that with me there should be yea yea, and nay nay?

title: II Corinthians 1:18
text: But [as] God [is] true, our word toward you was not yea and nay. {word: or, preaching}

title: II Corinthians 1:19
text: For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was preached among you by us, [even] by me and Silvanus and Timotheus, was not yea and nay, but in him was yea.

title: II Corinthians 1:20
text: For all the promises of God in him [are] yea, and in him Amen, unto the glory of God by us.

title: II Corinthians 1:21
text: Now he which stablisheth us with you in Christ, and hath anointed us, [is] God;

title: II Corinthians 1:22
text: Who hath also sealed us, and given the earnest of the Spirit in our hearts.

title: II Corinthians 1:23
text: Moreover I call God for a record upon my soul, that to spare you I came not as yet unto Corinth.

title: II Corinthians 1:24
text: Not for that we have dominion over your faith, but are helpers of your joy: for by faith ye stand.

title: II Corinthians 2:1
text: ¶But I determined this with myself, that I would not come again to you in heaviness.

title: II Corinthians 2:2
text: For if I make you sorry, who is he then that maketh me glad, but the same which is made sorry by me?

title: II Corinthians 2:3
text: And I wrote this same unto you, lest, when I came, I should have sorrow from them of whom I ought to rejoice; having confidence in you all, that my joy is [the joy] of you all.

title: II Corinthians 2:4
text: For out of much affliction and anguish of heart I wrote unto you with many tears; not that ye should be grieved, but that ye might know the love which I have more abundantly unto you.

title: II Corinthians 2:5
text: ¶But if any have caused grief, he hath not grieved me, but in part: that I may not overcharge you all.

title: II Corinthians 2:6
text: Sufficient to such a man [is] this punishment, which [was inflicted] of many. {punishment: or, censure}

title: II Corinthians 2:7
text: So that contrariwise ye [ought] rather to forgive [him], and comfort [him], lest perhaps such a one should be swallowed up with overmuch sorrow.

title: II Corinthians 2:8
text: Wherefore I beseech you that ye would confirm [your] love toward him.

title: II Corinthians 2:9
text: For to this end also did I write, that I might know the proof of you, whether ye be obedient in all things.

title: II Corinthians 2:10
text: To whom ye forgive any thing, I [forgive] also: for if I forgave any thing, to whom I forgave [it], for your sakes [forgave I it] in the person of Christ; {person: or, sight}

title: II Corinthians 2:11
text: Lest Satan should get an advantage of us: for we are not ignorant of his devices.

title: II Corinthians 2:12
text: ¶Furthermore, when I came to Troas to [preach] Christ's gospel, and a door was opened unto me of the Lord,

title: II Corinthians 2:13
text: I had no rest in my spirit, because I found not Titus my brother: but taking my leave of them, I went from thence into Macedonia.

title: II Corinthians 2:14
text: Now thanks [be] unto God, which always causeth us to triumph in Christ, and maketh manifest the savour of his knowledge by us in every place.

title: II Corinthians 2:15
text: For we are unto God a sweet savour of Christ, in them that are saved, and in them that perish:

title: II Corinthians 2:16
text: To the one [we are] the savour of death unto death; and to the other the savour of life unto life. And who [is] sufficient for these things?

title: II Corinthians 2:17
text: For we are not as many, which corrupt the word of God: but as of sincerity, but as of God, in the sight of God speak we in Christ. {corrupt: or, deal deceitfully with} {in Christ: or, of Christ}

title: II Corinthians 3:1
text: ¶Do we begin again to commend ourselves? or need we, as some [others], epistles of commendation to you, or [letters] of commendation from you?

title: II Corinthians 3:2
text: Ye are our epistle written in our hearts, known and read of all men:

title: II Corinthians 3:3
text: [Forasmuch as ye are] manifestly declared to be the epistle of Christ ministered by us, written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God; not in tables of stone, but in fleshy tables of the heart.

title: II Corinthians 3:4
text: And such trust have we through Christ to God-ward:

title: II Corinthians 3:5
text: Not that we are sufficient of ourselves to think any thing as of ourselves; but our sufficiency [is] of God;

title: II Corinthians 3:6
text: ¶Who also hath made us able ministers of the new testament; not of the letter, but of the spirit: for the letter killeth, but the spirit giveth life. {giveth life: or, quickeneth}

title: II Corinthians 3:7
text: But if the ministration of death, written [and] engraven in stones, was glorious, so that the children of Israel could not stedfastly behold the face of Moses for the glory of his countenance; which [glory] was to be done away:

title: II Corinthians 3:8
text: How shall not the ministration of the spirit be rather glorious?

title: II Corinthians 3:9
text: For if the ministration of condemnation [be] glory, much more doth the ministration of righteousness exceed in glory.

title: II Corinthians 3:10
text: For even that which was made glorious had no glory in this respect, by reason of the glory that excelleth.

title: II Corinthians 3:11
text: For if that which is done away [was] glorious, much more that which remaineth [is] glorious.

title: II Corinthians 3:12
text: ¶Seeing then that we have such hope, we use great plainness of speech: {plainness: or, boldness}

title: II Corinthians 3:13
text: And not as Moses, [which] put a vail over his face, that the children of Israel could not stedfastly look to the end of that which is abolished:

title: II Corinthians 3:14
text: But their minds were blinded: for until this day remaineth the same vail untaken away in the reading of the old testament; which [vail] is done away in Christ.

title: II Corinthians 3:15
text: But even unto this day, when Moses is read, the vail is upon their heart.

title: II Corinthians 3:16
text: Nevertheless when it shall turn to the Lord, the vail shall be taken away.

title: II Corinthians 3:17
text: Now the Lord is that Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord [is], there [is] liberty.

title: II Corinthians 3:18
text: But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory, [even] as by the Spirit of the Lord. {by the...: or, of the Lord the Spirit}

title: II Corinthians 4:1
text: ¶Therefore seeing we have this ministry, as we have received mercy, we faint not;

title: II Corinthians 4:2
text: But have renounced the hidden things of dishonesty, not walking in craftiness, nor handling the word of God deceitfully; but by manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every man's conscience in the sight of God. {dishonesty: Gr. shame}

title: II Corinthians 4:3
text: But if our gospel be hid, it is hid to them that are lost:

title: II Corinthians 4:4
text: In whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine unto them.

title: II Corinthians 4:5
text: For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus' sake.

title: II Corinthians 4:6
text: For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts, to [give] the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ. {hath: Gr. is he who hath}

title: II Corinthians 4:7
text: But we have this treasure in earthen vessels, that the excellency of the power may be of God, and not of us.

title: II Corinthians 4:8
text: ¶[We are] troubled on every side, yet not distressed; [we are] perplexed, but not in despair; {in despair: or, altogether without help, or, means}

title: II Corinthians 4:9
text: Persecuted, but not forsaken; cast down, but not destroyed;

title: II Corinthians 4:10
text: Always bearing about in the body the dying of the Lord Jesus, that the life also of Jesus might be made manifest in our body.

title: II Corinthians 4:11
text: For we which live are alway delivered unto death for Jesus' sake, that the life also of Jesus might be made manifest in our mortal flesh.

title: II Corinthians 4:12
text: So then death worketh in us, but life in you.

title: II Corinthians 4:13
text: We having the same spirit of faith, according as it is written, I believed, and therefore have I spoken; we also believe, and therefore speak;

title: II Corinthians 4:14
text: Knowing that he which raised up the Lord Jesus shall raise up us also by Jesus, and shall present [us] with you.

title: II Corinthians 4:15
text: For all things [are] for your sakes, that the abundant grace might through the thanksgiving of many redound to the glory of God.

title: II Corinthians 4:16
text: For which cause we faint not; but though our outward man perish, yet the inward [man] is renewed day by day.

title: II Corinthians 4:17
text: For our light affliction, which is but for a moment, worketh for us a far more exceeding [and] eternal weight of glory;

title: II Corinthians 4:18
text: While we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen: for the things which are seen [are] temporal; but the things which are not seen [are] eternal.

title: II Corinthians 5:1
text: ¶For we know that if our earthly house of [this] tabernacle were dissolved, we have a building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.

title: II Corinthians 5:2
text: For in this we groan, earnestly desiring to be clothed upon with our house which is from heaven:

title: II Corinthians 5:3
text: If so be that being clothed we shall not be found naked.

title: II Corinthians 5:4
text: For we that are in [this] tabernacle do groan, being burdened: not for that we would be unclothed, but clothed upon, that mortality might be swallowed up of life.

title: II Corinthians 5:5
text: Now he that hath wrought us for the selfsame thing [is] God, who also hath given unto us the earnest of the Spirit.

title: II Corinthians 5:6
text: Therefore [we are] always confident, knowing that, whilst we are at home in the body, we are absent from the Lord:

title: II Corinthians 5:7
text: (For we walk by faith, not by sight:)

title: II Corinthians 5:8
text: We are confident, [I say], and willing rather to be absent from the body, and to be present with the Lord.

title: II Corinthians 5:9
text: Wherefore we labour, that, whether present or absent, we may be accepted of him. {labour: or, endeavour}

title: II Corinthians 5:10
text: For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; that every one may receive the things [done] in [his] body, according to that he hath done, whether [it be] good or bad.

title: II Corinthians 5:11
text: Knowing therefore the terror of the Lord, we persuade men; but we are made manifest unto God; and I trust also are made manifest in your consciences.

title: II Corinthians 5:12
text: ¶For we commend not ourselves again unto you, but give you occasion to glory on our behalf, that ye may have somewhat to [answer] them which glory in appearance, and not in heart. {in appearance: Gr. in the face}

title: II Corinthians 5:13
text: For whether we be beside ourselves, [it is] to God: or whether we be sober, [it is] for your cause.

title: II Corinthians 5:14
text: For the love of Christ constraineth us; because we thus judge, that if one died for all, then were all dead:

title: II Corinthians 5:15
text: And [that] he died for all, that they which live should not henceforth live unto themselves, but unto him which died for them, and rose again.

title: II Corinthians 5:16
text: ¶Wherefore henceforth know we no man after the flesh: yea, though we have known Christ after the flesh, yet now henceforth know we [him] no more.

title: II Corinthians 5:17
text: Therefore if any man [be] in Christ, [he is] a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new. {he is: or, let him be}

title: II Corinthians 5:18
text: And all things [are] of God, who hath reconciled us to himself by Jesus Christ, and hath given to us the ministry of reconciliation;

title: II Corinthians 5:19
text: To wit, that God was in Christ, reconciling the world unto himself, not imputing their trespasses unto them; and hath committed unto us the word of reconciliation. {committed...: Gr. put in us}

title: II Corinthians 5:20
text: Now then we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God did beseech [you] by us: we pray [you] in Christ's stead, be ye reconciled to God.

title: II Corinthians 5:21
text: For he hath made him [to be] sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him.

title: II Corinthians 6:1
text: ¶We then, [as] workers together [with him], beseech [you] also that ye receive not the grace of God in vain.

title: II Corinthians 6:2
text: (For he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now [is] the accepted time; behold, now [is] the day of salvation.)

title: II Corinthians 6:3
text: Giving no offence in any thing, that the ministry be not blamed:

title: II Corinthians 6:4
text: But in all [things] approving ourselves as the ministers of God, in much patience, in afflictions, in necessities, in distresses, {approving: Gr. commending}

title: II Corinthians 6:5
text: In stripes, in imprisonments, in tumults, in labours, in watchings, in fastings; {in tumults: or, in tossings to and fro}

title: II Corinthians 6:6
text: By pureness, by knowledge, by longsuffering, by kindness, by the Holy Ghost, by love unfeigned,

title: II Corinthians 6:7
text: By the word of truth, by the power of God, by the armour of righteousness on the right hand and on the left,

title: II Corinthians 6:8
text: By honour and dishonour, by evil report and good report: as deceivers, and [yet] true;

title: II Corinthians 6:9
text: As unknown, and [yet] well known; as dying, and, behold, we live; as chastened, and not killed;

title: II Corinthians 6:10
text: As sorrowful, yet alway rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, and [yet] possessing all things.

title: II Corinthians 6:11
text: ¶O [ye] Corinthians, our mouth is open unto you, our heart is enlarged.

title: II Corinthians 6:12
text: Ye are not straitened in us, but ye are straitened in your own bowels.

title: II Corinthians 6:13
text: Now for a recompence in the same, (I speak as unto [my] children,) be ye also enlarged.

title: II Corinthians 6:14
text: Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers: for what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness? and what communion hath light with darkness?

title: II Corinthians 6:15
text: And what concord hath Christ with Belial? or what part hath he that believeth with an infidel?

title: II Corinthians 6:16
text: And what agreement hath the temple of God with idols? for ye are the temple of the living God; as God hath said, I will dwell in them, and walk in [them]; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.

title: II Corinthians 6:17
text: Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord, and touch not the unclean [thing]; and I will receive you,

title: II Corinthians 6:18
text: And will be a Father unto you, and ye shall be my sons and daughters, saith the Lord Almighty.

title: II Corinthians 7:1
text: ¶Having therefore these promises, dearly beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from all filthiness of the flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.

title: II Corinthians 7:2
text: Receive us; we have wronged no man, we have corrupted no man, we have defrauded no man.

title: II Corinthians 7:3
text: I speak not [this] to condemn [you]: for I have said before, that ye are in our hearts to die and live with [you].

title: II Corinthians 7:4
text: Great [is] my boldness of speech toward you, great [is] my glorying of you: I am filled with comfort, I am exceeding joyful in all our tribulation.

title: II Corinthians 7:5
text: ¶For, when we were come into Macedonia, our flesh had no rest, but we were troubled on every side; without [were] fightings, within [were] fears.

title: II Corinthians 7:6
text: Nevertheless God, that comforteth those that are cast down, comforted us by the coming of Titus;

title: II Corinthians 7:7
text: And not by his coming only, but by the consolation wherewith he was comforted in you, when he told us your earnest desire, your mourning, your fervent mind toward me; so that I rejoiced the more.

title: II Corinthians 7:8
text: For though I made you sorry with a letter, I do not repent, though I did repent: for I perceive that the same epistle hath made you sorry, though [it were] but for a season.

title: II Corinthians 7:9
text: Now I rejoice, not that ye were made sorry, but that ye sorrowed to repentance: for ye were made sorry after a godly manner, that ye might receive damage by us in nothing. {after...: or, according to God}

title: II Corinthians 7:10
text: For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world worketh death.

title: II Corinthians 7:11
text: For behold this selfsame thing, that ye sorrowed after a godly sort, what carefulness it wrought in you, yea, [what] clearing of yourselves, yea, [what] indignation, yea, [what] fear, yea, [what] vehement desire, yea, [what] zeal, yea, [what] revenge! In all [things] ye have approved yourselves to be clear in this matter.

title: II Corinthians 7:12
text: ¶Wherefore, though I wrote unto you, [I did it] not for his cause that had done the wrong, nor for his cause that suffered wrong, but that our care for you in the sight of God might appear unto you.

title: II Corinthians 7:13
text: Therefore we were comforted in your comfort: yea, and exceedingly the more joyed we for the joy of Titus, because his spirit was refreshed by you all.

title: II Corinthians 7:14
text: For if I have boasted any thing to him of you, I am not ashamed; but as we spake all things to you in truth, even so our boasting, which [I made] before Titus, is found a truth.

title: II Corinthians 7:15
text: And his inward affection is more abundant toward you, whilst he remembereth the obedience of you all, how with fear and trembling ye received him. {inward...: Gr. bowels}

title: II Corinthians 7:16
text: I rejoice therefore that I have confidence in you in all [things].

title: II Corinthians 8:1
text: ¶Moreover, brethren, we do you to wit of the grace of God bestowed on the churches of Macedonia;

title: II Corinthians 8:2
text: How that in a great trial of affliction the abundance of their joy and their deep poverty abounded unto the riches of their liberality. {liberality: Gr. simplicity}

title: II Corinthians 8:3
text: For to [their] power, I bear record, yea, and beyond [their] power [they were] willing of themselves;

title: II Corinthians 8:4
text: Praying us with much intreaty that we would receive the gift, and [take upon us] the fellowship of the ministering to the saints.

title: II Corinthians 8:5
text: And [this they did], not as we hoped, but first gave their own selves to the Lord, and unto us by the will of God.

title: II Corinthians 8:6
text: Insomuch that we desired Titus, that as he had begun, so he would also finish in you the same grace also. {grace: or, gift}

title: II Corinthians 8:7
text: ¶Therefore, as ye abound in every [thing, in] faith, and utterance, and knowledge, and [in] all diligence, and [in] your love to us, [see] that ye abound in this grace also.

title: II Corinthians 8:8
text: I speak not by commandment, but by occasion of the forwardness of others, and to prove the sincerity of your love.

title: II Corinthians 8:9
text: For ye know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that, though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, that ye through his poverty might be rich.

title: II Corinthians 8:10
text: And herein I give [my] advice: for this is expedient for you, who have begun before, not only to do, but also to be forward a year ago. {forward: Gr. willing}

title: II Corinthians 8:11
text: Now therefore perform the doing [of it]; that as [there was] a readiness to will, so [there may be] a performance also out of that which ye have.

title: II Corinthians 8:12
text: For if there be first a willing mind, [it is] accepted according to that a man hath, [and] not according to that he hath not.

title: II Corinthians 8:13
text: For [I mean] not that other men be eased, and ye burdened:

title: II Corinthians 8:14
text: But by an equality, [that] now at this time your abundance [may be a supply] for their want, that their abundance also may be [a supply] for your want: that there may be equality:

title: II Corinthians 8:15
text: As it is written, He that [had gathered] much had nothing over; and he that [had gathered] little had no lack.

title: II Corinthians 8:16
text: ¶But thanks [be] to God, which put the same earnest care into the heart of Titus for you.

title: II Corinthians 8:17
text: For indeed he accepted the exhortation; but being more forward, of his own accord he went unto you.

title: II Corinthians 8:18
text: And we have sent with him the brother, whose praise [is] in the gospel throughout all the churches;

title: II Corinthians 8:19
text: And not [that] only, but who was also chosen of the churches to travel with us with this grace, which is administered by us to the glory of the same Lord, and [declaration of] your ready mind: {grace: or, gift}

title: II Corinthians 8:20
text: Avoiding this, that no man should blame us in this abundance which is administered by us:

title: II Corinthians 8:21
text: Providing for honest things, not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of men.

title: II Corinthians 8:22
text: And we have sent with them our brother, whom we have oftentimes proved diligent in many things, but now much more diligent, upon the great confidence which [I have] in you. {I have: or, he hath}

title: II Corinthians 8:23
text: Whether [any do enquire] of Titus, [he is] my partner and fellowhelper concerning you: or our brethren [be enquired of, they are] the messengers of the churches, [and] the glory of Christ.

title: II Corinthians 8:24
text: Wherefore shew ye to them, and before the churches, the proof of your love, and of our boasting on your behalf.

title: II Corinthians 9:1
text: ¶For as touching the ministering to the saints, it is superfluous for me to write to you:

title: II Corinthians 9:2
text: For I know the forwardness of your mind, for which I boast of you to them of Macedonia, that Achaia was ready a year ago; and your zeal hath provoked very many.

title: II Corinthians 9:3
text: Yet have I sent the brethren, lest our boasting of you should be in vain in this behalf; that, as I said, ye may be ready:

title: II Corinthians 9:4
text: Lest haply if they of Macedonia come with me, and find you unprepared, we (that we say not, ye) should be ashamed in this same confident boasting.

title: II Corinthians 9:5
text: Therefore I thought it necessary to exhort the brethren, that they would go before unto you, and make up beforehand your bounty, whereof ye had notice before, that the same might be ready, as [a matter of] bounty, and not as [of] covetousness. {bounty: Gr. blessing} {whereof...: or, which hath been so much spoken of before}

title: II Corinthians 9:6
text: ¶But this [I say], He which soweth sparingly shall reap also sparingly; and he which soweth bountifully shall reap also bountifully.

title: II Corinthians 9:7
text: Every man according as he purposeth in his heart, [so let him give]; not grudgingly, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver.

title: II Corinthians 9:8
text: And God [is] able to make all grace abound toward you; that ye, always having all sufficiency in all [things], may abound to every good work:

title: II Corinthians 9:9
text: (As it is written, He hath dispersed abroad; he hath given to the poor: his righteousness remaineth for ever.

title: II Corinthians 9:10
text: Now he that ministereth seed to the sower both minister bread for [your] food, and multiply your seed sown, and increase the fruits of your righteousness;)

title: II Corinthians 9:11
text: Being enriched in every thing to all bountifulness, which causeth through us thanksgiving to God. {bountifulness: or, liberality: Gr. simplicity}

title: II Corinthians 9:12
text: For the administration of this service not only supplieth the want of the saints, but is abundant also by many thanksgivings unto God;

title: II Corinthians 9:13
text: Whiles by the experiment of this ministration they glorify God for your professed subjection unto the gospel of Christ, and for [your] liberal distribution unto them, and unto all [men];

title: II Corinthians 9:14
text: And by their prayer for you, which long after you for the exceeding grace of God in you.

title: II Corinthians 9:15
text: Thanks [be] unto God for his unspeakable gift.

title: II Corinthians 10:1
text: ¶Now I Paul myself beseech you by the meekness and gentleness of Christ, who in presence [am] base among you, but being absent am bold toward you: {in presence: or, in outward appearance}

title: II Corinthians 10:2
text: But I beseech [you], that I may not be bold when I am present with that confidence, wherewith I think to be bold against some, which think of us as if we walked according to the flesh. {think: or, reckon}

title: II Corinthians 10:3
text: For though we walk in the flesh, we do not war after the flesh:

title: II Corinthians 10:4
text: (For the weapons of our warfare [are] not carnal, but mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds;) {through God: or, to God}

title: II Corinthians 10:5
text: Casting down imaginations, and every high thing that exalteth itself against the knowledge of God, and bringing into captivity every thought to the obedience of Christ; {imaginations: or, reasonings}

title: II Corinthians 10:6
text: And having in a readiness to revenge all disobedience, when your obedience is fulfilled.

title: II Corinthians 10:7
text: ¶Do ye look on things after the outward appearance? If any man trust to himself that he is Christ's, let him of himself think this again, that, as he [is] Christ's, even so [are] we Christ's.

title: II Corinthians 10:8
text: For though I should boast somewhat more of our authority, which the Lord hath given us for edification, and not for your destruction, I should not be ashamed:

title: II Corinthians 10:9
text: That I may not seem as if I would terrify you by letters.

title: II Corinthians 10:10
text: For [his] letters, say they, [are] weighty and powerful; but [his] bodily presence [is] weak, and [his] speech contemptible. {say they: Gr. saith he}

title: II Corinthians 10:11
text: Let such an one think this, that, such as we are in word by letters when we are absent, such [will we be] also in deed when we are present.

title: II Corinthians 10:12
text: ¶For we dare not make ourselves of the number, or compare ourselves with some that commend themselves: but they measuring themselves by themselves, and comparing themselves among themselves, are not wise. {are...: or, understand it not}

title: II Corinthians 10:13
text: But we will not boast of things without [our] measure, but according to the measure of the rule which God hath distributed to us, a measure to reach even unto you. {rule: or, line}

title: II Corinthians 10:14
text: For we stretch not ourselves beyond [our measure], as though we reached not unto you: for we are come as far as to you also in [preaching] the gospel of Christ:

title: II Corinthians 10:15
text: Not boasting of things without [our] measure, [that is], of other men's labours; but having hope, when your faith is increased, that we shall be enlarged by you according to our rule abundantly, {enlarged...: or, magnified in you}

title: II Corinthians 10:16
text: To preach the gospel in the [regions] beyond you, [and] not to boast in another man's line of things made ready to our hand. {line: or, rule}

title: II Corinthians 10:17
text: But he that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord.

title: II Corinthians 10:18
text: For not he that commendeth himself is approved, but whom the Lord commendeth.

title: II Corinthians 11:1
text: ¶Would to God ye could bear with me a little in [my] folly: and indeed bear with me. {indeed bear...: or, indeed ye do bear with me}

title: II Corinthians 11:2
text: For I am jealous over you with godly jealousy: for I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present [you as] a chaste virgin to Christ.

title: II Corinthians 11:3
text: But I fear, lest by any means, as the serpent beguiled Eve through his subtilty, so your minds should be corrupted from the simplicity that is in Christ.

title: II Corinthians 11:4
text: For if he that cometh preacheth another Jesus, whom we have not preached, or [if] ye receive another spirit, which ye have not received, or another gospel, which ye have not accepted, ye might well bear with [him]. {with him: or, with me}

title: II Corinthians 11:5
text: ¶For I suppose I was not a whit behind the very chiefest apostles.

title: II Corinthians 11:6
text: But though [I be] rude in speech, yet not in knowledge; but we have been throughly made manifest among you in all things.

title: II Corinthians 11:7
text: Have I committed an offence in abasing myself that ye might be exalted, because I have preached to you the gospel of God freely?

title: II Corinthians 11:8
text: I robbed other churches, taking wages [of them], to do you service.

title: II Corinthians 11:9
text: And when I was present with you, and wanted, I was chargeable to no man: for that which was lacking to me the brethren which came from Macedonia supplied: and in all [things] I have kept myself from being burdensome unto you, and [so] will I keep [myself].

title: II Corinthians 11:10
text: As the truth of Christ is in me, no man shall stop me of this boasting in the regions of Achaia. {no man...: Gr. this boasting shall not be stopped in me}

title: II Corinthians 11:11
text: Wherefore? because I love you not? God knoweth.

title: II Corinthians 11:12
text: But what I do, that I will do, that I may cut off occasion from them which desire occasion; that wherein they glory, they may be found even as we.

title: II Corinthians 11:13
text: For such [are] false apostles, deceitful workers, transforming themselves into the apostles of Christ.

title: II Corinthians 11:14
text: And no marvel; for Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light.

title: II Corinthians 11:15
text: Therefore [it is] no great thing if his ministers also be transformed as the ministers of righteousness; whose end shall be according to their works.

title: II Corinthians 11:16
text: ¶I say again, Let no man think me a fool; if otherwise, yet as a fool receive me, that I may boast myself a little. {receive: or, suffer}

title: II Corinthians 11:17
text: That which I speak, I speak [it] not after the Lord, but as it were foolishly, in this confidence of boasting.

title: II Corinthians 11:18
text: Seeing that many glory after the flesh, I will glory also.

title: II Corinthians 11:19
text: For ye suffer fools gladly, seeing ye [yourselves] are wise.

title: II Corinthians 11:20
text: For ye suffer, if a man bring you into bondage, if a man devour [you], if a man take [of you], if a man exalt himself, if a man smite you on the face.

title: II Corinthians 11:21
text: I speak as concerning reproach, as though we had been weak. Howbeit whereinsoever any is bold, (I speak foolishly,) I am bold also.

title: II Corinthians 11:22
text: ¶Are they Hebrews? so [am] I. Are they Israelites? so [am] I. Are they the seed of Abraham? so [am] I.

title: II Corinthians 11:23
text: Are they ministers of Christ? (I speak as a fool) I [am] more; in labours more abundant, in stripes above measure, in prisons more frequent, in deaths oft.

title: II Corinthians 11:24
text: Of the Jews five times received I forty [stripes] save one.

title: II Corinthians 11:25
text: Thrice was I beaten with rods, once was I stoned, thrice I suffered shipwreck, a night and a day I have been in the deep;

title: II Corinthians 11:26
text: [In] journeyings often, [in] perils of waters, [in] perils of robbers, [in] perils by [mine own] countrymen, [in] perils by the heathen, [in] perils in the city, [in] perils in the wilderness, [in] perils in the sea, [in] perils among false brethren;

title: II Corinthians 11:27
text: In weariness and painfulness, in watchings often, in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, in cold and nakedness.

title: II Corinthians 11:28
text: Beside those things that are without, that which cometh upon me daily, the care of all the churches.

title: II Corinthians 11:29
text: Who is weak, and I am not weak? who is offended, and I burn not?

title: II Corinthians 11:30
text: If I must needs glory, I will glory of the things which concern mine infirmities.

title: II Corinthians 11:31
text: The God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, which is blessed for evermore, knoweth that I lie not.

title: II Corinthians 11:32
text: In Damascus the governor under Aretas the king kept the city of the Damascenes with a garrison, desirous to apprehend me:

title: II Corinthians 11:33
text: And through a window in a basket was I let down by the wall, and escaped his hands.

title: II Corinthians 12:1
text: ¶It is not expedient for me doubtless to glory. I will come to visions and revelations of the Lord. {I will come: Gr. For I will come}

title: II Corinthians 12:2
text: I knew a man in Christ above fourteen years ago, (whether in the body, I cannot tell; or whether out of the body, I cannot tell: God knoweth;) such an one caught up to the third heaven.

title: II Corinthians 12:3
text: And I knew such a man, (whether in the body, or out of the body, I cannot tell: God knoweth;)

title: II Corinthians 12:4
text: How that he was caught up into paradise, and heard unspeakable words, which it is not lawful for a man to utter. {lawful: or, possible}

title: II Corinthians 12:5
text: Of such an one will I glory: yet of myself I will not glory, but in mine infirmities.

title: II Corinthians 12:6
text: For though I would desire to glory, I shall not be a fool; for I will say the truth: but [now] I forbear, lest any man should think of me above that which he seeth me [to be], or [that] he heareth of me.

title: II Corinthians 12:7
text: And lest I should be exalted above measure through the abundance of the revelations, there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, the messenger of Satan to buffet me, lest I should be exalted above measure.

title: II Corinthians 12:8
text: For this thing I besought the Lord thrice, that it might depart from me.

title: II Corinthians 12:9
text: And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me.

title: II Corinthians 12:10
text: Therefore I take pleasure in infirmities, in reproaches, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses for Christ's sake: for when I am weak, then am I strong.

title: II Corinthians 12:11
text: ¶I am become a fool in glorying; ye have compelled me: for I ought to have been commended of you: for in nothing am I behind the very chiefest apostles, though I be nothing.

title: II Corinthians 12:12
text: Truly the signs of an apostle were wrought among you in all patience, in signs, and wonders, and mighty deeds.

title: II Corinthians 12:13
text: For what is it wherein ye were inferior to other churches, except [it be] that I myself was not burdensome to you? forgive me this wrong.

title: II Corinthians 12:14
text: Behold, the third time I am ready to come to you; and I will not be burdensome to you: for I seek not yours, but you: for the children ought not to lay up for the parents, but the parents for the children.

title: II Corinthians 12:15
text: And I will very gladly spend and be spent for you; though the more abundantly I love you, the less I be loved. {for you: Gr. for your souls}

title: II Corinthians 12:16
text: But be it so, I did not burden you: nevertheless, being crafty, I caught you with guile.

title: II Corinthians 12:17
text: Did I make a gain of you by any of them whom I sent unto you?

title: II Corinthians 12:18
text: I desired Titus, and with [him] I sent a brother. Did Titus make a gain of you? walked we not in the same spirit? [walked we] not in the same steps?

title: II Corinthians 12:19
text: Again, think ye that we excuse ourselves unto you? we speak before God in Christ: but [we do] all things, dearly beloved, for your edifying.

title: II Corinthians 12:20
text: For I fear, lest, when I come, I shall not find you such as I would, and [that] I shall be found unto you such as ye would not: lest [there be] debates, envyings, wraths, strifes, backbitings, whisperings, swellings, tumults:

title: II Corinthians 12:21
text: [And] lest, when I come again, my God will humble me among you, and [that] I shall bewail many which have sinned already, and have not repented of the uncleanness and fornication and lasciviousness which they have committed.

title: II Corinthians 13:1
text: ¶This [is] the third [time] I am coming to you. In the mouth of two or three witnesses shall every word be established.

title: II Corinthians 13:2
text: I told you before, and foretell you, as if I were present, the second time; and being absent now I write to them which heretofore have sinned, and to all other, that, if I come again, I will not spare:

title: II Corinthians 13:3
text: Since ye seek a proof of Christ speaking in me, which to you-ward is not weak, but is mighty in you.

title: II Corinthians 13:4
text: For though he was crucified through weakness, yet he liveth by the power of God. For we also are weak in him, but we shall live with him by the power of God toward you. {in him: or, with him}

title: II Corinthians 13:5
text: Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves. Know ye not your own selves, how that Jesus Christ is in you, except ye be reprobates?

title: II Corinthians 13:6
text: But I trust that ye shall know that we are not reprobates.

title: II Corinthians 13:7
text: ¶Now I pray to God that ye do no evil; not that we should appear approved, but that ye should do that which is honest, though we be as reprobates.

title: II Corinthians 13:8
text: For we can do nothing against the truth, but for the truth.

title: II Corinthians 13:9
text: For we are glad, when we are weak, and ye are strong: and this also we wish, [even] your perfection. {perfection: or, reformation, or, restoration}

title: II Corinthians 13:10
text: Therefore I write these things being absent, lest being present I should use sharpness, according to the power which the Lord hath given me to edification, and not to destruction.

title: II Corinthians 13:11
text: ¶Finally, brethren, farewell. Be perfect, be of good comfort, be of one mind, live in peace; and the God of love and peace shall be with you.

title: II Corinthians 13:12
text: Greet one another with an holy kiss.

title: II Corinthians 13:13
text: All the saints salute you.

title: II Corinthians 13:14
text: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Ghost, [be] with you all. Amen. <<[The second [epistle] to the Corinthians was written from Philippi, [a city] of Macedonia, by Titus and Lucas.]>>

title: Galatians 1:1
text: ¶Paul, an apostle, (not of men, neither by man, but by Jesus Christ, and God the Father, who raised him from the dead;)

title: Galatians 1:2
text: And all the brethren which are with me, unto the churches of Galatia:

title: Galatians 1:3
text: Grace [be] to you and peace from God the Father, and [from] our Lord Jesus Christ,

title: Galatians 1:4
text: Who gave himself for our sins, that he might deliver us from this present evil world, according to the will of God and our Father:

title: Galatians 1:5
text: To whom [be] glory for ever and ever. Amen.

title: Galatians 1:6
text: ¶I marvel that ye are so soon removed from him that called you into the grace of Christ unto another gospel:

title: Galatians 1:7
text: Which is not another; but there be some that trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ.

title: Galatians 1:8
text: But though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed.

title: Galatians 1:9
text: As we said before, so say I now again, If any [man] preach any other gospel unto you than that ye have received, let him be accursed.

title: Galatians 1:10
text: ¶For do I now persuade men, or God? or do I seek to please men? for if I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ.

title: Galatians 1:11
text: But I certify you, brethren, that the gospel which was preached of me is not after man.

title: Galatians 1:12
text: For I neither received it of man, neither was I taught [it], but by the revelation of Jesus Christ.

title: Galatians 1:13
text: For ye have heard of my conversation in time past in the Jews' religion, how that beyond measure I persecuted the church of God, and wasted it:

title: Galatians 1:14
text: And profited in the Jews' religion above many my equals in mine own nation, being more exceedingly zealous of the traditions of my fathers. {equals: Gr. equals in years}

title: Galatians 1:15
text: But when it pleased God, who separated me from my mother's womb, and called [me] by his grace,

title: Galatians 1:16
text: To reveal his Son in me, that I might preach him among the heathen; immediately I conferred not with flesh and blood:

title: Galatians 1:17
text: Neither went I up to Jerusalem to them which were apostles before me; but I went into Arabia, and returned again unto Damascus.

title: Galatians 1:18
text: Then after three years I went up to Jerusalem to see Peter, and abode with him fifteen days. {went up: or, returned}

title: Galatians 1:19
text: But other of the apostles saw I none, save James the Lord's brother.

title: Galatians 1:20
text: Now the things which I write unto you, behold, before God, I lie not.

title: Galatians 1:21
text: Afterwards I came into the regions of Syria and Cilicia;

title: Galatians 1:22
text: And was unknown by face unto the churches of Judaea which were in Christ:

title: Galatians 1:23
text: But they had heard only, That he which persecuted us in times past now preacheth the faith which once he destroyed.

title: Galatians 1:24
text: And they glorified God in me.

title: Galatians 2:1
text: ¶Then fourteen years after I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, and took Titus with [me] also.

title: Galatians 2:2
text: And I went up by revelation, and communicated unto them that gospel which I preach among the Gentiles, but privately to them which were of reputation, lest by any means I should run, or had run, in vain. {privately: or, severally}

title: Galatians 2:3
text: But neither Titus, who was with me, being a Greek, was compelled to be circumcised:

title: Galatians 2:4
text: And that because of false brethren unawares brought in, who came in privily to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage:

title: Galatians 2:5
text: To whom we gave place by subjection, no, not for an hour; that the truth of the gospel might continue with you.

title: Galatians 2:6
text: But of these who seemed to be somewhat, (whatsoever they were, it maketh no matter to me: God accepteth no man's person:) for they who seemed [to be somewhat] in conference added nothing to me:

title: Galatians 2:7
text: But contrariwise, when they saw that the gospel of the uncircumcision was committed unto me, as [the gospel] of the circumcision [was] unto Peter;

title: Galatians 2:8
text: (For he that wrought effectually in Peter to the apostleship of the circumcision, the same was mighty in me toward the Gentiles:)

title: Galatians 2:9
text: And when James, Cephas, and John, who seemed to be pillars, perceived the grace that was given unto me, they gave to me and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship; that we [should go] unto the heathen, and they unto the circumcision.

title: Galatians 2:10
text: Only [they would] that we should remember the poor; the same which I also was forward to do.

title: Galatians 2:11
text: ¶But when Peter was come to Antioch, I withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed.

title: Galatians 2:12
text: For before that certain came from James, he did eat with the Gentiles: but when they were come, he withdrew and separated himself, fearing them which were of the circumcision.

title: Galatians 2:13
text: And the other Jews dissembled likewise with him; insomuch that Barnabas also was carried away with their dissimulation.

title: Galatians 2:14
text: But when I saw that they walked not uprightly according to the truth of the gospel, I said unto Peter before [them] all, If thou, being a Jew, livest after the manner of Gentiles, and not as do the Jews, why compellest thou the Gentiles to live as do the Jews?

title: Galatians 2:15
text: We [who are] Jews by nature, and not sinners of the Gentiles,

title: Galatians 2:16
text: Knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ, and not by the works of the law: for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified.

title: Galatians 2:17
text: But if, while we seek to be justified by Christ, we ourselves also are found sinners, [is] therefore Christ the minister of sin? God forbid.

title: Galatians 2:18
text: For if I build again the things which I destroyed, I make myself a transgressor.

title: Galatians 2:19
text: For I through the law am dead to the law, that I might live unto God.

title: Galatians 2:20
text: I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me: and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me.

title: Galatians 2:21
text: I do not frustrate the grace of God: for if righteousness [come] by the law, then Christ is dead in vain.

title: Galatians 3:1
text: ¶O foolish Galatians, who hath bewitched you, that ye should not obey the truth, before whose eyes Jesus Christ hath been evidently set forth, crucified among you?

title: Galatians 3:2
text: This only would I learn of you, Received ye the Spirit by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith?

title: Galatians 3:3
text: Are ye so foolish? having begun in the Spirit, are ye now made perfect by the flesh?

title: Galatians 3:4
text: Have ye suffered so many things in vain? if [it be] yet in vain. {so many: or, so great}

title: Galatians 3:5
text: He therefore that ministereth to you the Spirit, and worketh miracles among you, [doeth he it] by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith?

title: Galatians 3:6
text: ¶Even as Abraham believed God, and it was accounted to him for righteousness. {accounted: or, imputed}

title: Galatians 3:7
text: Know ye therefore that they which are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham.

title: Galatians 3:8
text: And the scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith, preached before the gospel unto Abraham, [saying], In thee shall all nations be blessed.

title: Galatians 3:9
text: So then they which be of faith are blessed with faithful Abraham.

title: Galatians 3:10
text: For as many as are of the works of the law are under the curse: for it is written, Cursed [is] every one that continueth not in all things which are written in the book of the law to do them.

title: Galatians 3:11
text: But that no man is justified by the law in the sight of God, [it is] evident: for, The just shall live by faith.

title: Galatians 3:12
text: And the law is not of faith: but, The man that doeth them shall live in them.

title: Galatians 3:13
text: Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us: for it is written, Cursed [is] every one that hangeth on a tree:

title: Galatians 3:14
text: That the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ; that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.

title: Galatians 3:15
text: Brethren, I speak after the manner of men; Though [it be] but a man's covenant, yet [if it be] confirmed, no man disannulleth, or addeth thereto. {covenant: or, testament}

title: Galatians 3:16
text: Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ.

title: Galatians 3:17
text: And this I say, [that] the covenant, that was confirmed before of God in Christ, the law, which was four hundred and thirty years after, cannot disannul, that it should make the promise of none effect.

title: Galatians 3:18
text: For if the inheritance [be] of the law, [it is] no more of promise: but God gave [it] to Abraham by promise.

title: Galatians 3:19
text: ¶Wherefore then [serveth] the law? It was added because of transgressions, till the seed should come to whom the promise was made; [and it was] ordained by angels in the hand of a mediator.

title: Galatians 3:20
text: Now a mediator is not [a mediator] of one, but God is one.

title: Galatians 3:21
text: [Is] the law then against the promises of God? God forbid: for if there had been a law given which could have given life, verily righteousness should have been by the law.

title: Galatians 3:22
text: But the scripture hath concluded all under sin, that the promise by faith of Jesus Christ might be given to them that believe.

title: Galatians 3:23
text: But before faith came, we were kept under the law, shut up unto the faith which should afterwards be revealed.

title: Galatians 3:24
text: Wherefore the law was our schoolmaster [to bring us] unto Christ, that we might be justified by faith.

title: Galatians 3:25
text: But after that faith is come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster.

title: Galatians 3:26
text: For ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus.

title: Galatians 3:27
text: For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ.

title: Galatians 3:28
text: There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus.

title: Galatians 3:29
text: And if ye [be] Christ's, then are ye Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise.

title: Galatians 4:1
text: ¶Now I say, [That] the heir, as long as he is a child, differeth nothing from a servant, though he be lord of all;

title: Galatians 4:2
text: But is under tutors and governors until the time appointed of the father.

title: Galatians 4:3
text: Even so we, when we were children, were in bondage under the elements of the world: {elements: or, rudiments}

title: Galatians 4:4
text: But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law,

title: Galatians 4:5
text: To redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons.

title: Galatians 4:6
text: And because ye are sons, God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father.

title: Galatians 4:7
text: Wherefore thou art no more a servant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir of God through Christ.

title: Galatians 4:8
text: ¶Howbeit then, when ye knew not God, ye did service unto them which by nature are no gods.

title: Galatians 4:9
text: But now, after that ye have known God, or rather are known of God, how turn ye again to the weak and beggarly elements, whereunto ye desire again to be in bondage? {turn ye again: or, turn ye back} {elements: or, rudiments}

title: Galatians 4:10
text: Ye observe days, and months, and times, and years.

title: Galatians 4:11
text: I am afraid of you, lest I have bestowed upon you labour in vain.

title: Galatians 4:12
text: ¶Brethren, I beseech you, be as I [am]; for I [am] as ye [are]: ye have not injured me at all.

title: Galatians 4:13
text: Ye know how through infirmity of the flesh I preached the gospel unto you at the first.

title: Galatians 4:14
text: And my temptation which was in my flesh ye despised not, nor rejected; but received me as an angel of God, [even] as Christ Jesus.

title: Galatians 4:15
text: Where is then the blessedness ye spake of? for I bear you record, that, if [it had been] possible, ye would have plucked out your own eyes, and have given them to me. {Where...: or, What was then}

title: Galatians 4:16
text: Am I therefore become your enemy, because I tell you the truth?

title: Galatians 4:17
text: ¶They zealously affect you, [but] not well; yea, they would exclude you, that ye might affect them. {exclude you: or, exclude us}

title: Galatians 4:18
text: But [it is] good to be zealously affected always in [a] good [thing], and not only when I am present with you.

title: Galatians 4:19
text: ¶My little children, of whom I travail in birth again until Christ be formed in you,

title: Galatians 4:20
text: I desire to be present with you now, and to change my voice; for I stand in doubt of you. {I stand...: or, I am perplexed for you}

title: Galatians 4:21
text: ¶Tell me, ye that desire to be under the law, do ye not hear the law?

title: Galatians 4:22
text: For it is written, that Abraham had two sons, the one by a bondmaid, the other by a freewoman.

title: Galatians 4:23
text: But he [who was] of the bondwoman was born after the flesh; but he of the freewoman [was] by promise.

title: Galatians 4:24
text: Which things are an allegory: for these are the two covenants; the one from the mount Sinai, which gendereth to bondage, which is Agar. {covenants: or, testaments} {Sinai: Gr. Sina}

title: Galatians 4:25
text: For this Agar is mount Sinai in Arabia, and answereth to Jerusalem which now is, and is in bondage with her children. {answereth to: or, is in the same rank with}

title: Galatians 4:26
text: But Jerusalem which is above is free, which is the mother of us all.

title: Galatians 4:27
text: For it is written, Rejoice, [thou] barren that bearest not; break forth and cry, thou that travailest not: for the desolate hath many more children than she which hath an husband.

title: Galatians 4:28
text: Now we, brethren, as Isaac was, are the children of promise.

title: Galatians 4:29
